There is no way I can write this review without giving Russell, the owner of Body Cycle, a shout out. Russell's passion for fitness and cycling is so evident, as is his desire for all of his clients to succeed. He is always dropping in to classes to check in/provide encouragement, and is open to ideas and recommendations from anyone. Russell always wears a smile on his face, even when he's kicking your butt in class!

input: Loved this tour! I grabbed a groupon and the price was great. input:
My experience with Shalimar was nothing but wonderful. 
I wanted to get my engagement ring sized and was told over the phone that it could probably be done within the day. 
When I brought it by, the team confirmed that the jeweler would be able to accommodate my same-day request and that it would be around $40 (simple band, decrease by three full sizes).
I checked my size one more time, confirmed, and left to let them do their thing.
When I came to pick up later that afternoon, the ring was too small. It's very important to note that Shalimar sized the ring perfectly, but that I made a mistake and should've gone up a half-size.
The Shalimar group were completely understanding and accommodating, even resizing my ring back up and getting it back to me within an hour at no charge! Even though it was my mistake!
The associates' attitudes in dealing with what was a pretty embarrassing situation instantly earned my satisfaction and loyalty as a customer. Very grateful for such a wonderful experience.
Rewrite this for me:
My visit to Shalimar was an absolutely wonderful experience. I needed my engagement ring resized and was initially told over the phone it might be possible the same day. Upon arriving, the team confirmed their jeweler could accommodate me, quoting approximately $40 for the work—a simple band needing to be reduced by three sizes. I double-checked my size, confirmed it, and left the ring with them.

That afternoon, when I returned, the ring was unfortunately too tight. Crucially, Shalimar had sized it perfectly to my initial instruction; the error was mine, as I realized I actually needed an extra half-size. Despite this being my mistake, the team was completely understanding and accommodating. They promptly resized the ring upward and had it back to me within an hour, refusing to charge for the additional work.

The associates’ gracious and professional handling of an embarrassing situation instantly secured my satisfaction and loyalty. I am deeply grateful for such exceptional service.

input:

The hot dog itself is flavorful, but I would prefer that it or the bacon have a little more bite or snap to better hold their own against the dominant mustard and onions. 

I'm with the masses on the carne asada caramelo. Excellent tortilla, salty, melty cheese, and great carne. 

Super cheap and you can drive through.
Rewrite this for me:

input:
I was really between 3 and 4 stars for this one. I LOVE the 96th street Naked Tchopstix so I was very excited to see this one which is closer to my house.
The vibe is totally different as this is geared more to take out although they do have a decent size dining area. You order at the counter and they deliver it.
My daughter and I tried the sushi bowl. You pick up a piece of paper and  select from a choice of proteins, vegetables, rice and toppings. I like the fact that it is on paper and you don't have to guess what things are or have to shout over the counter to tell the server what you want. The sushi bowl was good but not wonderful. The choices particularly of the vegetables seemed a little too limiting and I felt I had more rice than other food items. The sauces were tasty. My husband ordered the Maui roll which is my favorite roll at the 96th street location and this just was not up that standard. It was good but the quality and consistently was not as good as at 96th street. I would go back though and I think a lot of people would be happy with the sushi bowls. I do want to make a comment about the low reviews that people have given the place because of service. People - it is a sushi place - it isn't McDonalds- so it will be a bit slower. You are not going to order and get out of there in five minutes even though it is called express. As a healthy alternative to fast food in the area, it is worth the wait. Oh and try the bubble tea. I had the strawberry and it was quite yummy. Next time I am going to try the vanilla chai.
Rewrite this for me:
I debated between a three and four-star rating for this location. As a big fan of the 96th Street Naked Tchopstix, I was eager to try this branch, which is more convenient for me.

The atmosphere here is completely different, as the setup is geared more toward takeout. They do have a reasonably sized dining area, but you order at the counter and your food is brought to you. My daughter and I tried the build-your-own sushi bowl. You select from a list of proteins, vegetables, rice, and toppings on a paper menu. I appreciated this system—it’s clear, you don’t have to guess what’s available, and you don’t need to shout your order across the counter.

The sushi bowl was good, though not exceptional. The vegetable choices felt somewhat limited, and my bowl seemed to contain more rice than other components. The sauces, however, were quite tasty. My husband ordered the Maui roll, which is my favorite at the 96th Street location. While still good, it didn’t meet the same standard in terms of quality and consistency.

I would return, and I believe many would be satisfied with the sushi bowls as a healthy, customizable option. I also want to address some of the lower reviews criticizing the service speed. This is a sushi spot, not fast food like McDonald’s, so orders understandably take a bit more time. Even with “Express” in the name, don’t expect to be in and out in five minutes. As a healthier alternative in the area, it’s worth the short wait.

Lastly, don’t skip the bubble tea. I tried the strawberry flavor and found it delicious. Next time, I’m looking forward to sampling the vanilla chai.

Our accommodations were in the Tuscany Tower on the 12th floor, offering a pleasant overlook of the expansive pool complex. The room was spacious and well-appointed, featuring free WiFi, a large bathroom with dual sinks, ample counter space, a two-headed shower, a jetted tub, and even a phone beside the commode. The good: price, location, dessert (edible food items are: baked chicken, fried chicken, mashed potatoes, Salad bar lol, meat and cheese bar, ravioli, pizza) also our waitress was bomb af

The meh: behind counter meat slicing station, shrimp (not even deveined), Mexican station

The bad: breakfast -worst eggs ever, actually worst, eggs. Le Benedict can't even cut through ham or English muffin (tried on all 3 occasions), steak, shrimp again, hell breaded items can't even, don't even. Decor it's the 1970 nightmare you can imagine

Tried 3 times and failed
Rewrite this for me:
This buffet is inexpensive, but the quality matches the price.

The positives are the low cost, convenient location, and a few edible items like the baked chicken, fried chicken, mashed potatoes, and pizza. Our waitress was also excellent.

The mediocre offerings include the meat-slicing station and the Mexican station. The shrimp, notably, were not even deveined.

The worst elements were the breakfast—specifically the terrible eggs—and failed dishes like the uncuttable Eggs Benedict, poor steak, and soggy breaded items. The decor is a dated 1970s nightmare.

We gave it three chances, and each visit was a disappointment.

input:
The only reason I didn't give this restaurant a 5 star rating, is because of one single pretentious waiter. As a 4 night guest at Hotel Palomar, the location of the restaurant is an obvious plus. The first night of my stay, I met a coworker in the restaurant for a cocktail. When we arrived, the host staff were busy and not available, so we just walked in. The restaurant was not too busy, so we just looked at a small table next to the bar and proceeded to take a seat. A waiter came by and I quickly asked if we could have a seat, before sitting down and told him we'd only be having cocktails. He stumbled on his reply, and in an irritated/in-convinced tone, told me "I guess it would be fine" and basically just kept walking mid sentence. My guest and I brushed it off, and started having a conversation while looking at the drink menu. To make a long story short, he was distant and we both got the "couldn't be bothered" vibe from him. When it came to the bill, we asked if it could be split due to company transaction policies, and you would have thought asked him for some inconceivable task. We basically spent the rest of our night and elevator ride to our room in shock of the rudeness we had just experienced. 

Although that situation left a bad taste in our mouth, and the night before we decided to avoid the restaurant, we decided to grab another cocktail and give this place one more try. After looking around and ensuring "last nights waiter" wasn't on shift, we walked over to the bar and started looking over the menu. Instantly, the bartender greeted us with pleasant small talk and made us feel 100% welcome. He asked about our day, recommended cocktails and was a completely genuine person. This guy (I think his name was Ben) is an absolute star! He gave us lessons on Whiskey, described how to make classic cocktails, and was 100% invested in our experience. This is exactly what a bartender at a 4/5 star establishment should be - actually he exceeds that. He was kind, funny, friendly and completely redeemed this restaurant/bar from our terrible experience the night before. 
I also ordered room service last night from this restaurant, and it was amazing. The bacon wrapped dates and chocolate cake are to die for! Great restaurant and amazing bartender(s). Too bad one bad egg could have spoiled this experience.
Rewrite this for me:
My sole reason for withholding a five-star rating is a single, pretentious waiter. As a guest at Hotel Palomar for four nights, the restaurant’s location was a clear convenience. On my first evening, I met a coworker there for a cocktail. Upon arrival, the host stand was unattended, so we walked in. Seeing the space wasn’t busy, we approached a small table near the bar. Before sitting, I quickly asked a passing waiter if it was alright, explaining we only wanted drinks. He stumbled over his reply and, in an irritated and unconvinced tone, said, “I guess it would be fine,” essentially walking away mid-sentence. My guest and I brushed it off, but his distant demeanor gave us a palpable “couldn’t be bothered” vibe throughout. When we requested the bill be split for company expense purposes, he reacted as if we’d asked for something inconceivable. We spent the rest of the night, including the elevator ride to our room, in shock at such outright rudeness.

That encounter left a bad taste, and we avoided the restaurant the next night. However, on our final evening, we decided to give it one more try for a cocktail. After scanning the room to ensure that particular waiter wasn’t on shift, we approached the bar. Instantly, the bartender—I believe his name was Ben—greeted us with warm small talk, making us feel completely welcome. He asked about our day, offered excellent cocktail recommendations, and was utterly genuine. Ben is an absolute star. He gave us impromptu lessons on whiskey, explained how classic cocktails are crafted, and was fully invested in our experience. This is precisely what a bartender at a quality establishment should be—in fact, he exceeds that standard. His kind, funny, and friendly nature completely redeemed the restaurant and bar from our terrible prior experience.

I should also note that I ordered room service from the restaurant last night, and it was exceptional. The bacon-wrapped dates and the chocolate cake are to die for. Ultimately, this is a great restaurant with amazing bartenders. It’s just a shame that one bad egg nearly spoiled the entire experience.

input: NEVER AGAIN. This is a so called restaurant that does nothing that a restaurant should other than prepare food, because the rest is done by the patron. Want water? Get up and go across the yard to get it. Want a drink, walk up a flight of stairs and pay cash. Want to sit in a dirty yard in dirty lawn chairs, enjoy yourself. The wait staff is mildy helpful in that they bring you your food after you go to the window and pay cash for it...kind of like New Orleans Hamburger and Seafood, but dirty and with live music (which is nice). It's a one in a lifetime experience for me...just once.
Rewrite this for me: NEVER AGAIN. This establishment barely qualifies as a restaurant, as it delegates nearly every responsibility to the customer. Patrons must fetch their own water from across the yard, climb stairs to purchase drinks with cash, and sit in a grimy courtyard on dirty lawn chairs. The only service is staff delivering food after you pay cash at a window—a model reminiscent of New Orleans Hamburger and Seafood, but far less sanitary. While the live music was pleasant, the overall experience was profoundly disappointing. For me, this is a one-time occurrence; a single visit is more than enough.

input:
If you want to pay for everything a la carte this is the place for you.  
Food wasn't terrible not impressive.
They brought a basket of chips and some tomato sauce which I asked politely for something spicier and some pico de gallo.  She brought them happily to me and the salsa was much better.  When asked what we would like to drink I asked for a coke and she brought out a bottle which I stated I wanted the fountain drink.  She said "oh that's only Pepsi".  Never mentioned that they only had bottle drinks for coke.  
We ordered our food which was reasonably priced, asked for sour cream and also to put cheese on the taco.  She let us know cheese was extra.  
It was $2.50 extra for another basket of chips.  
When I received the bill we paid more for the condiments then the actual food.  Side of sour cream 2.00, pico de gallo 2.50, salsa 2.00, chips 2.50, cheese 1.00 and the bottled coke that we didn't want 5.00.  
Just a suggestion...when you order anything make sure to ask if there is an extra charge.
Rewrite this for me:
This restaurant operates on a strictly à la carte basis, so be prepared to pay separately for each item. The food itself was acceptable—neither terrible nor impressive.

Service was pleasant; when I politely requested something spicer than the provided tomato sauce, the server happily brought pico de gallo and a better salsa. However, the pricing approach was not always clear upfront. I ordered a Coke and was brought a bottle; only when I asked for a fountain drink did she mention they only serve Pepsi that way, without initially stating bottled Coke carried a different charge.

Our reasonably priced meal order included requests for sour cream and cheese on a taco. We were informed the cheese was extra. An additional basket of chips was $2.50.

The final bill revealed the issue: we paid more for condiments and add-ons than the core food. Charges included sour cream ($2.00), pico de gallo ($2.50), salsa ($2.00), the extra chips ($2.50), cheese ($1.00), and the unwanted bottled Coke ($5.00).

My strong suggestion: before ordering anything here, always ask if there is an extra charge.

input:
On a scale of one to things that are awesome, this place is the bomb. 

I was drawn in by the promise of the duckfat frenchfries. Took the boy for his birthday and put our name in, had a drink around the corner while we waited and were given seats at the bar after about 45 minutes. 

We were waited on by Keith, the bartender, who was congenial, knowledgeable about his whiskeys and an all-around cool guy. We started with 3 cape may salts (two for me, one for the boy) and tater tots, both of which made me happy.

For dinner, I got Kentucky Fried Quail (stellar, though the succotash was not as exciting as I wanted it to be) and the boy got the 24$ Fois Gras burger, which was incredible. Worth every penny. The duckfat fries were pretty yummy, but not even the best part of the meal. I could've done without the cheese sauce, but as it was on the side I wasn't deterred.

I look forward to coming back here, with everyone I know.
Rewrite this for me:
On a scale of one to awesome, this restaurant is absolutely top-tier.

The initial lure for me was the famous duck fat fries. I took my son for his birthday; we put our name on the list, had a drink nearby during the 45-minute wait, and were eventually seated at the bar.

Our bartender, Keith, provided excellent service. He was friendly, deeply knowledgeable about whiskey, and just an all-around great guy. We began with three Cape May Salts (two for me, one for my son) and an order of tater tots—both were fantastic starters.

For our mains, I had the Kentucky Fried Quail. It was stellar, though the accompanying succotash was a bit underwhelming. My son ordered the $24 Foie Gras Burger, which was utterly incredible and worth every cent. As for the famed duck fat fries? They were delicious, but surprisingly not the meal's highlight. The optional cheese sauce was unnecessary for me, but since it was on the side, it was no issue.

I can’t wait to return and bring everyone I know.

input: It was my fiance's birthday and he decided he wanted a good, laid back Thai restaurant for dinner. Yelp steered us in the Jasmine Rice direction, and it was definitely a good decision. We wanted the summer rolls, which were on the menu, but apparently will not be available until summer, so we settled on the pan-fried dumplings. The flavor was good, but I don't think we'd order them again. We got the green curry fried rice with duck and chicken pad thai. Both of those dishes were great, but the duck stole the show. That was some the of tastiest duck I've ever had. The pad thai was a bit sweet for us, so I think we'd try a different noodle dish when we return. But it was still very good, especially with some chili sauce mixed in. Our service was good, but other people had issues. One table was rushing to get to a show at the Kimmel Center and waited quite a while for their meal (and were going to be late). Another person who got take-out was missing one of their items (but the owner realized it and called him and walked the dish to his house, which was very nice). Overall, good quality Thai! We would definitely go back.
Rewrite this for me:
For my fiancé’s birthday, he wanted a relaxed Thai dinner. Following a Yelp recommendation, we chose Jasmine Rice—a decision we didn’t regret. We initially hoped to try the summer rolls, but learned they’re only available in summer, so we opted for the pan-fried dumplings instead. They were flavorful, though not something we’d likely reorder.

For our mains, we selected the green curry fried rice with duck and the chicken pad thai. Both were excellent, but the duck was truly exceptional—some of the most delicious I’ve ever tasted. The pad thai leaned sweeter than we prefer, so next time we might try a different noodle dish. That said, it was still very good, especially once we mixed in some chili sauce.

Service was attentive for us, though we noticed hiccups elsewhere. One table, hurrying to a show at the Kimmel Center, faced a long wait and were likely late. Another customer’s takeout order was missing an item, but the owner personally realized the mistake, called the guest, and even walked the dish to his house—a very kind gesture.

Overall, Jasmine Rice offers solid, quality Thai food. We enjoyed our meal and will definitely return.

input:
My go to menu is coconut soup and pad thai with protein. I tried same menu here.

Pat thai was great too. Liked the amount of peanut they used, noodle was chewy and perfect and not too sweet. They gave me generous amount of chicken and white meat wasn't dry so I was very happy with my meal.
Rewrite this for me:
My usual order is coconut soup and pad thai with protein, which I tried here. I particularly enjoyed the soup; it was perfectly creamy from ample coconut milk and not overpowered by herbs. As someone accustomed to Americanized Thai food, I prefer milder herb flavors (cilantro aside).

The pad thai was also excellent. It featured a generous amount of peanut, perfectly chewy noodles, and a balanced sweetness. The portion of chicken was substantial, and the white meat remained moist, making for a very satisfying meal.

input:
We were a bit weary about trying the Shellfish Company on the Wharf as more often than not, many places like these (see Cannery Row, Monterey) feast on a captive audience and provide sub-standard fare at high prices.

However, emboldened by the perennial good reviews on Yelp, we suppressed our initial observations and went ahead with the trying it out. The place is small, so definitely plan ahead. You will have to wait, so either you know, just do so, or perhaps try to visit outside of peak hours. Luckily, our wait was only about 20 minutes as the dinner rush was just leveling off.

The special was the local rock crab - $25 for 3 lbs of California Rock Crab, salad, and your choice of soup/chowder. After taking a look at a few trays of rock crab being served out, the wife and I both opted for it, as it looked awesome.  

The salad/chowder combo was great as you actually received hearty portions of each, so it was a good start. As much as I liked the chowder however, the Shrimp Bisque the wife ordered was amazing, so I would recommend that going forward. 

But enough of prattling on about side dishes: the rock crab tasted just as glorious as it looked. Juicy, buttery chunks of white crab meat await you, just a few cracks away. While the rock crab shells are pretty thick, once cracked, they splinter and separate easily, a good sign they are cooked to perfection. The rock crabs provided a great amount of meat for what I felt to be the least amount of work you're going to do for crab, King or otherwise. 

We were thoroughly satisfied with our meal and along with the special being an overall great value, devouring the Rock Crab at SBSC turned out to be one of the favorite meals on the trip. I think ordering crab here is a safe proposition indeed.
Rewrite this for me:
We had our reservations about trying the Shellfish Company on the Wharf. Places like this in tourist areas—think Cannery Row in Monterey—often rely on a captive audience, serving mediocre food at inflated prices.

Nevertheless, consistently strong Yelp reviews encouraged us to set aside our skepticism and give it a try. The restaurant is quite small, so planning ahead is essential. Be prepared to wait; either accept that as part of the experience or aim for off-peak hours. We were fortunate, arriving as the dinner rush subsided, and were seated after about 20 minutes.

The special that night was local rock crab: three pounds for $25, served with a salad and a choice of soup or chowder. After seeing several impressive trays of crab delivered to other tables, my wife and I both decided to order it.

The meal began well with the salad and chowder—both portions were substantial and satisfying. While the chowder was good, my wife’s shrimp bisque was exceptional, and I’d highly recommend it.

But the true star was the rock crab. It lived up to its impressive appearance, offering juicy, buttery chunks of white meat that were just a few cracks away. Although the shells are sturdy, they split cleanly when cracked—a sure sign of perfect cooking. The crabs yielded a generous amount of meat for what felt like minimal effort, especially compared to tackling larger varieties like king crab.

We left thoroughly satisfied. Between the exceptional flavor and the notable value of the special, our rock crab feast at the Shellfish Company became one of the standout meals of our trip. Ordering crab here is not just a safe bet—it’s a genuinely rewarding one.

input: I LOVE Weaver's Way and really disagree with some of the content in previous reviews. WW is not necessarily meant for convenience shopping. I am a single woman and I find that I have no trouble shopping at the co-op, during peak times or otherwise. I actually find the co-op to be a great place to shop if you live alone because I can get smaller quantities of items than if I shop at the corporate stores like Acme. I also enjoy the work hours - I've worked throughout the store, but most recently, I have been getting in my hours by participating in the membership committee. I wouldn't say that the community is necessarily made up of "tree huggers" and "earth children", though. The community is made up of a variety of similarly-minded folks from different backgrounds. I enjoy having a place to go to where I can obtain locally grown produce, a place that offers more natural, wholesome, and preservative-free foods than chain stores with prices way below that of Whole Foods. I enjoy interacting with other members and contributing to my local and global community. I don't find the membership fee or the work hours to be prohibitive being a single person vs. a family. I don't think that membership in a co-op is for everyone and, if you aren't single, it's definitely not a solo decision. If you're keen on being committed to the Weaver Way values, you couldn't find a better place to shop. If not, stick to the chain stores or just pay the 10% visitors' fee to pop in once in a while.
Rewrite this for me:
I am a devoted fan of Weaver’s Way and feel compelled to offer a different perspective from some earlier reviews. It’s important to understand that the co-op isn’t designed primarily for convenience. As a single person, I shop there regularly—during busy times and slow ones—without issue. In fact, it’s ideal for living alone, as I can purchase smaller, more manageable quantities than at corporate supermarkets like Acme.

I also value the member work requirement. I’ve worked in various store roles and currently serve on the membership committee, which I find rewarding. While some might stereotype the community, it isn’t just “tree huggers” or “earth children.” It’s a diverse group of like-minded individuals from all walks of life.

What I treasure most is access to locally grown produce and more natural, preservative-free foods than conventional chains offer—all at prices significantly lower than Whole Foods. I enjoy connecting with fellow members and knowing my participation supports both local and global communities. Neither the membership fee nor the work hours feel prohibitive to me as a single person versus a family.

That said, a co-op isn’t for everyone. If you have a household, joining is a shared decision, not a solo one. But if you genuinely align with Weaver’s Way values, there’s no better place to shop. If not, you can always stick to chain stores or visit occasionally and pay the 10% non-member fee.

input:
After living in the STL area for way over 10 years now, I am both ashamed and remorseful to admit that I ate here for the FIRST time just a few weeks ago. I am ashamed because it's a St. Louis tradition and remorseful because I missed out on it for so..many...years! 

This place is amazing. What is not to love! It's a factory where you can get a tour (Friday-Sunday, noon-5pm on the hour), there's a shop, bar, and dining area. They also host many event with live music on the weekends. It's fun to just kind of wander and look around - don't worry, you'll get a chance because there will likely be a wait before you dine. For better quality and price, I’d recommend Superior Seafood during their happy hour for $0.50 oysters. The turtle soup had an odd flavor—I prefer Felix’s version. I would return for the sheer convenience if I’m in the area again, likely for a quick seafood pickup, but not primarily for the dining experience.

input: We stayed at The Saint last year for a girl's trip. The lobby is lovely, they have a cool bar and restaurant that you can't help but to "ohh and ahh" over when you walk in. My friend arrived, and our evening began. After a fun dinner out, we returned to the room, laughing and ready to unwind. That’s when we saw it: a massive flying roach. I was horrified. I immediately walked down to the front desk and insisted they address it. The onion rings - a little greasy, but very tasty and crisp. The onions stayed in the breading and didn't slide out when you bit them (which I hate). 

Spanakopita - mine was a little over cooked, but the flavors were really good

Baklava - VERY GOOD! 

Signature Salad - The veggies they use are very fresh which will make or break a salad. Their balsamic is great too!

The (turkey) Greek Burger - one of the best turkey burgers I've ever had! The patty was moist and flavorful all on its own, but then they top it with what must be homemade tzatziki. input:
Went here based on the high ratings and raves from people.  The entire experience was underwhelming from start to finish.  Their website which is fairly useless if you want to figure out the menu before going, you have to pick your location choice out of 3 locations and then drill down to the bottom to see the weak descriptions of their menu offering, no explanations and no price, just this

    Roast Beef
    Roast Beef Combo
    Roast Pork
    Roast Pork Combo
    Baked Ham
    Baked Ham Combo
    Roast Turkey
    Roast Turkey Combo
    Broccoli Rabe
    Broccoli Rabe Combo


No explanation of whats in a combo (its just where they add cheese by the way)

The table placecard (instead of menu) had a more detailed description than the website.  

When I walked in, its more bar than restaurant, no big deal, but there were tables.  Since I couldnt decide and the sandwiches werent too expensive at $6.85, I got the roast beef and roast port combos.

I got my two sandwiches fast enough, but the roast beef was cold and the roast pork was hot.  Not sure how a cook (for lack of a better word) could serve 2 things at the same time with such a temperature differential, one was obviously sitting for awhile.  I asked the waitress to reheat the roast beef while I finished the roast pork, and supposedly it was reheated, since it was warmer, but it was still cold-ish compared to my roast pork I had just finished.  The waitress did offer to replace it when she inquired, but I was in a hurry and didnt really care for a hot version of this sandwich.

The sandwiches were very skimpy on meat, but they "made up for it" by adding too much gravy to make it overly messy and the bread was disintegrating.  The menu place card mentions the "wet meat" option where you get less gravy, I strongly recommend you get it that style, especially if the gravy overpower the meat and structural integrity of the sandwich.
Rewrite this for me:
I chose this restaurant based on its high ratings and enthusiastic reviews, but the entire experience proved underwhelming. The problems began with their website, which is nearly useless for previewing the menu. You must first select one of three locations, then scroll to the bottom to find a list with weak descriptions, no explanations, and no prices. It simply displays items like “Roast Beef,” “Roast Beef Combo,” and “Roast Pork Combo,” without clarifying what a “combo” includes (it merely adds cheese, by the way).

The physical table placard, which served as the menu, offered more detail than the website. Upon entering, I noted the space felt more like a bar than a restaurant, though tables were available. Since I couldn’t decide and the sandwiches were reasonably priced at $6.85, I ordered both a roast beef combo and a roast pork combo.

The sandwiches arrived quickly, but immediately there was an issue: the roast beef was cold while the roast pork was hot. It was puzzling how two items served simultaneously could have such a temperature discrepancy, suggesting one had been sitting out. I asked the waitress to reheat the roast beef while I ate the pork. It returned warmer but still noticeably cooler than the pork I had just finished. She kindly offered a replacement, but I was pressed for time and had lost my appetite for a hot version.

Furthermore, the sandwiches were surprisingly skimpy on meat. This was poorly compensated for by an excessive amount of gravy, which made them overly messy and caused the bread to disintegrate. The menu placard mentions a “wet meat” option for less gravy; I strongly recommend choosing that style. Otherwise, the gravy overwhelms both the flavor of the meat and the structural integrity of the sandwich itself.

input:
Too big, too expensive and too far from Downtown.  

I was here for a conference, which seemed like an awesome idea. It wasn't.  I'm in Direct Sales and (like most people at this conference) don't have tons of extra money to spend on mediocre meals when I'm traveling.  $10 for a slice of generic pizza, small side salad and a soda for lunch.   I understand it's a hotel but there weren't any options close by.  Just getting your car from valet was a hassle and took a lot of time.  Being such a big property, it made getting to restaurants off the property really time intensive.  Since you're so far out of Nashville (out near the airport), the good little holes you find when you're in a city are pretty nonexistent.  

The property itself was great.  The hotel is HUGE but really pretty.  I enjoyed walking around but was really happy when I found what I didn't know existed...a shortcut between my room and the Convention Center.  It took my 10-15 minute walk down to about 3 minutes!  BONUS!  Like I said, this place is ginormous.  

Room: Our room was great.  I shared a wonderful suite in the Garden Conservatory with 2 other girls.  We were under a group rate and my friend was quoted $200/night, which is awesome for the space we had.  We had a large room (probably used as a hospitality suite for groups) for socializing.  It had a great bar area set-up and a nice big fridge and lots of drawer space.  Our bedroom was separated by doors that could be locked from either side (like an adjoining room), so it looked like the hospitality suite could be reserved without reserving the room.  It was different than what I was expecting, but whatevs.  It was fine.  So, I wasn't there at check-in.  The girl who reserved the room checked in a couple days earlier than my friend and I.  So, Sunday comes, and the bill was waiting for us when we woke up.  Our friend was charged $1200 for one room (I'm guessing the suite) and $1400 for the other room.  YEP.  She reserved what she thought was a 2 room suite for $200.  The bedroom door was closed when she got there and she asked them to open it up. It was all arranged by the bellman.  She was never told that the bedroom wasn't included....kind of necessary if you're staying over for 6 nights, dontcha think???  So, she's being charged $2600 for what was supposed to be $1200.  Last I heard, the Gaylord's legal department was investigating what she was told, what she wasn't told and if they should charge her the entire amount.  

Checkout:  A FREAKING NIGHTMARE.  Between the money situation, which was not resolved as of late this week, and the 45 minute wait for a cart (in a hotel that holds thousands of people, you'd think they'd be plentiful and they aren't) and a 25 minute wait for the car, my friend and I decided to sweat it out and schlep our goods to the door where our car would be delivered to us.  It was not a short walk and we had a TON of stuff, which meant multiple trips.  UGH.

I'm sure I'll be back for another conference (I am pretty sure my company has booked this for at least one more year....) but I'm not going to be happy about it.  I might even consider driving down, staying in a hotel somewhere downtown and driving out to the Conference stuff.
Rewrite this for me:
Too large, too costly, and too distant from the city center.

I attended a conference here, which initially seemed like a fantastic plan. It wasn’t. I work in direct sales and, like most attendees, don’t have a lavish travel budget for overpriced, average food. Lunch—a slice of generic pizza, a small side salad, and a soda—cost $10. I recognize this is a hotel, but with no alternatives nearby, you’re stuck. Even retrieving your car from valet was a time-consuming hassle. The resort’s massive scale makes venturing off-property for meals a major undertaking. Given its location near the airport, far from downtown Nashville, the charming local eateries you’d typically seek out in a city simply don’t exist here.

The property itself is impressive. The hotel is enormous but truly beautiful. I enjoyed exploring, though I was thrilled to discover an unknown shortcut between my room and the convention center, reducing a 10–15 minute walk to about three minutes—a major bonus! As mentioned, the place is ginormous.

**The Room:** Our accommodations were great. I shared a lovely suite in the Garden Conservatory with two friends. We were on a group rate, and my friend was quoted $200 per night, which is excellent for the space. We had a large room (likely designed as a hospitality suite) for socializing, complete with a bar setup, a sizeable refrigerator, and ample drawer space. Our bedroom was separated by doors that locked from either side, like an adjoining room, suggesting the hospitality suite could be booked independently. It wasn’t what I expected, but it was fine. I wasn’t present at check-in; the friend who made the reservation arrived a few days earlier. On Sunday, the bill awaited us upon waking. She had been charged $1,200 for one room (the suite, I assume) and $1,400 for the other. Yes, you read that correctly. She had reserved what she believed was a two-room suite for $200. The bedroom door was closed upon her arrival, and she asked staff to open it, which a bellman arranged. At no point was she informed the bedroom wasn’t included—a rather crucial detail for a six-night stay, don’t you think? So, she’s being charged $2,600 for what was supposed to cost $1,200. The last I heard, the hotel’s legal department was investigating what she was and wasn’t told, and whether to charge her the full amount.

**Checkout:** An absolute nightmare. Between the unresolved billing issue and the logistics—a 45-minute wait for a luggage cart (shockingly scarce for a hotel hosting thousands) and a 25-minute wait for the car—my friend and I decided to sweat it out and haul our belongings to the door where the car would be delivered. It wasn’t a short walk, we had a ton of stuff, and it required multiple trips. Ugh.

I’ll likely return for another conference—my company has probably booked it for at least another year—but I won’t be happy about it. I’m even considering driving in, staying at a hotel downtown, and commuting to the conference events instead.

input:
This was my first time dining at Ava and I enjoyed most of it. We ordered the Ricotta cheese & toasted bread and although the flavor was excellent, I thought the bread to cheese ratio was off quite a bit. The ricotta came in a tiny ramekin typically reserved for flavored butters, so I expected more for an appetizer. 

The two pizzas split among a couple of people were the sausage and the potato with rosemary. They were both tasty but I think they forgot the Rosemary on ours. Still yummy, tho! Another entree was the grouper w/Israeli couscous. Scrumptious!

Dessert was a must and the zeppoles, or sugared donuts, were amazing. The cherry tart a little less so, but one person at our table loved it, so maybe it was just not my cup of tea. The cherries were a sort of candied cherry-interesting, but sweet with a very dense crust. Again, just not my personal fave. 

I will definitely return to try other menu items that looked great-like the pastas made in-house daily...that's next!!
Rewrite this for me:
My first visit to Ava was largely enjoyable. We started with the ricotta cheese and toasted bread. While the flavor was excellent, the portion balance felt off; the ricotta arrived in a very small ramekin, making the appetizer seem scant for sharing.

For our main courses, we shared two pizzas: the sausage and the potato. Both were tasty, though our potato pizza seemed to lack the promised rosemary. Another entrée, the grouper with Israeli couscous, was absolutely scrumptious.

Dessert was essential. The zeppoles—sugared donuts—were amazing. The cherry tart was less to my personal taste, though another diner adored it. I found the candied cherries very sweet and the crust quite dense, but it was simply a matter of preference.

I will certainly return to explore more of the menu, particularly the daily house-made pastas, which are next on my list to try.

input: REALLY below average food.  Akin to waffle house.  I wanted this to be good based on the reviews but not so. Rewrite this for me: The food was disappointingly below average, comparable to a Waffle House. Despite positive reviews, the pancakes tasted frozen and processed. The so-called "homemade" maple syrup was watery, overly sweet, and artificially flavored—real syrup comes from trees, not kitchens. The hash browns were greasy and bland, while the bacon was overcooked, hard, and chewy, clearly having sat out. Overall, the fare was uninspired. This spot seems to coast on an outdated "must-visit" reputation, while Nashville holds far better options.

input: Love this little shop so much for so many reasons. First off, whenever I'm on my way to Sweet Divas, I can smell the spices wafting from this little, inviting shop. Over the years I've purchased many items from here and I can attest that they do last a long time (about a year, year and a half, including some stuff I use often!). I see all kind of specialty salts for example (onion salt, celery salt) as well as sugars and powders (lavender vanilla sugar, vanilla bean powder). Their products even seem to taste fresher (I can taste a difference between their cinnamon and nutmeg and what I can get at a dollar store, for example). The prices aren't too bad and they last long. My three bottles pictured cost about $19, but that will last a good year, so its worth it to me.

While the variety might seem overwhelming, the knowledgeable and friendly staff are always ready to help you find the perfect spice for any culinary need.

Items like their cinnamon and nutmeg are far superior. Furthermore, their spices have excellent longevity, typically remaining vibrant for a year to a year and a half, even with regular use. The value is outstanding; for example, the three bottles I purchased cost around $19 and will easily last a year, making it a worthwhile investment for any home cook.

input: Went here with a friend after having an incredible experience at Laurel and was hoping for more of the same at a slightly less bulgy pricepoint, and oh my, is it worth it... We went on to eat many more things which i will try to name now... Stars were Foie with Apricot Miso, Pork Cheeks with some insanely good vegetables, trout pumpernickel soldiers and one of the best cocktails ive had in a damn long time, the ouroboros.   The are playing around with cold smoking things in there and on their BAR MENU!   Honestly, place is just terrific and i meant to write this review sooner but hey... better late than never.  Now that i think of it, im getting hungry... maybe ill head to East Passyunk for some of the best this city has to offer!

My friend and I came here hoping to replicate the incredible experience we’d had at Laurel, but at a slightly more accessible price—and oh my, it absolutely delivered. ITV is the kind of place I dream about: a beautiful, small, dimly lit room where you can still actually see everything (a welcome contrast to some overly dark spots). You *want* to see everything, too, because every detail is considered, including many of the staff (just painting the full picture here).

The meal began with a three-dollar beef fat biscuit that was, without exaggeration, the best thing I’ve eaten in this city all year. I made a point to tell that to Chef Nick Elmi himself, who was graciously present in the dining room, just as he was at Laurel.

We then enjoyed a parade of exceptional dishes. Standouts included the Foie with Apricot Miso, the Pork Cheeks with insanely good vegetables, and the trout pumpernickel soldiers. I also had one of the best cocktails in a damn long time: the Ouroboros. They’re even doing clever things with cold smoking, right on their bar menu!

Honestly, the place is just terrific. I meant to write this review sooner, but better late than never. Now that I think about it, I’m getting hungry again… maybe it’s time to head to East Passyunk for some more of the best this city has to offer.

Let me preface by saying that I have been getting my hair cut by a guy in Austin for seven years, even though I've lived in other cities for half that time. He is that good. The couple of times that I've strayed, I have been severely disappointed in the outcome. But I wasn't planning a trip back to Austin for a while and badly needed a cut, so I decided to bite the bullet.

My friend walks in a few weeks ago with *srsly* the cutest short hair cut. And so I ask her who and where, and she says Rodney Mitchell. I figured that this place would be too expensive, but she corrected my thinking on the matter. So I called to make an appointment with her guy (whose name I sadly cannot remember at the moment) and Rodney answered the phone. Turns out the guy my friend had seen didn't do morning appointments and all my afternoons were filled, so Rodney said "look, I'm the owner, I can absolutely vouch for Allison who has several openings in the next few days." So I thought, alright, he's the owner so he knows his stuff--I'll do it.

Allison absolutely did not disappoint. First off, she's a total sweetheart, but not super chatty (I appreciate stylists who can be content to both hold and not hold a convo while working) so there was no pressure there. I came in with my laptop and several photos I'd found that approximated what I wanted in a haircut, as I couldn't find exactly the right one. We talked about it a bit, discussed front and back length, bangs, etc. and she said alright and went to it. What she gave me was the cutest damn shaggy bob that I never thought possible. I seriously can't wait to go back.

One of the other awesome things about RMS is that they give you a discount for your first visit and I believe they have some kind of discount for students and teachers. They also will give you *another* discount when you refer people. So I got my friend a discount, and then referred a friend, so I'll get another discount when I go back for my next cut. All good things when you're trying your best to be a frugal  grad student.
Rewrite this for me:
For seven years, I’ve had my hair cut by the same stylist in Austin. He’s so good that I’ve kept returning to him even while living in other cities for half that time. My few attempts elsewhere always led to severe disappointment. Recently, however, a trip to Austin wasn’t on the horizon and I desperately needed a cut, so I decided to bite the bullet and try someone new locally.

The decision was made for me when a friend walked in with the *srsly* cutest short haircut. I immediately asked for the details, and she pointed me to Rodney Mitchell Salon. I assumed it would be too expensive, but she corrected that assumption. When I called to book with her specific stylist, Rodney himself answered. Unfortunately, that stylist didn’t do morning appointments, and my afternoons were completely booked. Rodney then said, “Look, I’m the owner, and I can absolutely vouch for Allison, who has several openings soon.” His confidence, as the owner, reassured me. I decided to trust his recommendation.

Allison absolutely did not disappoint. She is a total sweetheart and possesses the perfect demeanor—attentive but not overly chatty. I appreciate stylists who are comfortable with both conversation and comfortable silence, and she nailed that balance. I arrived prepared with my laptop and several photos that approximated my desired look, since I couldn’t find one perfect example. We discussed the front and back length, bangs, and overall shape. Once we aligned, she got to work. The result was the cutest damn shaggy bob I never thought possible for my hair. I was thrilled and already looking forward to my next appointment.

Another great aspect of Rodney Mitchell Salon is their thoughtful discount structure. They offer a discount for your first visit and, I believe, have special rates for students and teachers. They also run a referral program: when you refer someone, you receive a discount on your next service. So, I secured a discount for my friend who referred me, and after referring another friend, I’ll get a discount on my next cut. These perks are genuinely appreciated when you’re navigating life as a frugal grad student.

input:
So much to like about this place--the beautiful Mercer Building location, the spaciousness, the lovely, friendly baristas. But there are a couple of important cons for me. Biggest being, the music is constant and too loud, ruining everything you go to a coffee shop to do: read, work, reflect, or enjoy a good conversation. When I asked for it to be turned down, they told me they can't--it just plays at one level all the time, and the speakers  are everywhere so you can't get away from it. It sucks.

Secondly, if you're a tea drinker, you're out of luck. They don't serve the tea in pots, but huge, sloppy individual filters--it makes your beverage totally ungainly, hard to drink and is really off putting.

Pros: gluten free goodies and yummy Italian sodas. I'd love to spend more time here, but the music usually drives me out after 10 minutes.
Rewrite this for me:
There is much to admire here: the lovely Mercer Building setting, the spacious interior, and the genuinely friendly baristas. However, two significant drawbacks affect my experience. Primarily, the music is a constant, intrusive presence—too loud for reading, working, reflecting, or conversation. Upon requesting it be lowered, I was informed the system plays at one fixed volume through ubiquitous speakers, making escape impossible. It fundamentally undermines the coffee shop’s purpose.

Secondly, for tea drinkers, the serving method is a letdown. Instead of pots, they use oversized, sloppy individual filters, making the beverage awkward and difficult to enjoy.

input:
I've come from Cali where boba is very common there. However I was thinking this place would have had the same feel. After being told this place branched off from California, I was disappointed. 

I'm more of a natural person. I enjoy real flavor, real fruits, and of course the perfect boba. I notice that some flavors were used by real fruits but others were just powder which I could definitely taste the different. Especially the taro flavor, being one of my favorites. 

But, if you're not too concern about natural vs powder flavor then this place could be good for you. They ask what level you would like you sweetness and any additional add-ons you would like. I always get boba but sometimes the grass jelly is pretty good too! I'd recommend you try. 

This is also a good place to catch up, talk, play board, card games and even do homework. I know it's always busy with students from the U of A and being told from them it's a nice area to just hang out, that's a pretty good sign. 

Maybe I'm just too picky, but I think it could be better. 

"See it, taste it, Yelp it"

Coming from California, where boba is everywhere, I expected this spot to have a similar vibe—especially after hearing it was a branch of a West Coast chain. Sadly, it fell short of my hopes.

If you aren’t particular about natural versus artificial flavoring, you might still enjoy it. They let you customize sweetness and add toppings like boba or grass jelly—the latter is quite good sometimes. It’s worth a try.

The space itself is a plus. It’s popular with University of Arizona students for hanging out, studying, or playing games. The busy, social atmosphere is definitely a good sign.

Maybe I’m just picky, but I believe this place has room to improve.

"See it, taste it, Yelp it."

input:

input:
You think Value City, you think cheap value, right? Wrong! 

Think Rothman prices with Ashley Furniture pieces. Not a Broyhill in sight. 

Negatives:
- Entertainment centers and TV stand selection is small, and over priced selection.
-Their "Clearance" section is laughable and not much of a sale. No one is going to pay $299 for a nicked up coffee table that was originally $350. Go lower. 
- Sectionals by themselves average around $1,000 by brands I've never heard of. 
- The staff hangs out like a clique chatting in the middle of the store rather than helping customers. 
-Dining sets are nothing special and overpriced as well. I've seen the same selection everywhere else at a lower price. 
-5% military discount? Ooooh you're going to knock $20 off my sofa! 

Only Positive:
-They have a few modern pieces. 

Overall:

I think they're high for low quality-mediocre furniture. Shop around town. Or if you do find something you must have here, wait for a holiday sale.
Rewrite this for me:
Value City Furniture’s name suggests affordability, but the reality is quite different. The pricing often rivals that of high-end retailers, yet the showroom is filled with lesser-known brands and pieces comparable to Ashley Furniture, with no sign of quality names like Broyhill.

The store has significant drawbacks. The selection of entertainment centers and TV stands is limited and overpriced. The so-called “Clearance” section is ineffective, offering minimal savings on damaged goods. Sectionals from obscure brands average around $1,000. Dining sets are unremarkable and priced higher than competitors. Customer service is lacking, with staff often congregating instead of assisting shoppers. Even the 5% military discount is negligible on large purchases.

The sole positive is a small assortment of modern pieces. Overall, the store offers low to mediocre quality at premium prices. It’s advisable to shop around locally. If you must buy something here, wait for a major holiday sale to secure a fairer price.

input:

The katsu is great and I highly recommend it to people looking for a more filling dish on the menu. The bao buns were also good for a lighter fish. I haven't had anything I really regretted trying, but definitely ask your server about the portion sizes of each dish since they vary across the menu.

The cocktail selection is excellent. I even had a special Japanese Old Fashioned last time which was a little expensive, but well worth it for some quality Japanese whiskey. 

I'm looking forward to exploring the menu little by little. The best way to experience this is in a group setting so you can try more things and it really reminds me of Izakayas or Japanese pubs I visited in Japan and Korea.
Rewrite this for me:

For a hearty option, the katsu is excellent and highly recommended. The bao buns also stand out as a satisfying lighter choice. While I’ve enjoyed everything I’ve tried, I suggest inquiring about portion sizes, as they can vary significantly across the menu.

The cocktail list is superb. On my last visit, I sampled a special Japanese Old Fashioned. Though slightly pricey, it was well worth it for the quality of whiskey.

I look forward to gradually exploring more of the menu. This restaurant is best experienced in a group, allowing you to sample a wider variety—a style that authentically recalls the Izakayas and Japanese pubs I visited in Japan and Korea.

input: Very cozy place to have a drink with friends.  The drinks were tasty and were served in very pretty glasses reminiscent of those some of our grandmothers had in their china cabinets. Rewrite this for me: This is a wonderfully cozy spot for drinks with friends. For food, I tried the bacon-wrapped dates, which were disappointingly oversweetened, as if double-dipped in sugar, and I finished them out of hunger rather than enjoyment. While the servers were pleasant and attentively checked in, I wasn’t offered a second drink when my empty glass was cleared. A significant drawback was the noise; once about ten more people arrived, conversation became difficult despite the room’s many fabric surfaces.

As unassuming as it looks, this particular South Philly Mexican place is worth stopping by.

Upon opening one of my three tacos, I was immediately impressed: each contained an entire filet. The fish was flaky and without any overly “fishy” taste. The toppings leaned American—lettuce, tomato, and cheese—though I suspect cilantro and onion were available upon request. The sole staff member was cheerful and accommodating; then again, we were the only diners inside.

Another solid choice is the super-crispy chorizo taco, served with more traditional toppings and just $8 for three. Notably, there was no gristle—a common pitfall at such modest establishments.

Despite its utterly plain exterior, this South Philly Mexican spot is certainly worth a visit.

Peppermill, if you want to create a cool cocktail bar, ditch the machines, train your staff, or hire bartenders with better service skills, and buy some independent liquors.
Rewrite this for me:
Terrace Lounge at the Peppermill seems to aspire to be a notable cocktail destination, but it fails to meet that mark. The experience was disappointing on multiple fronts. For one, the bar staff appeared disorganized and underprepared; one bartender was even unaware of a new cocktail menu. The drink I received was weak and diluted, a problem compounded by the reliance on generic, corporate spirits found throughout the casino. Service was inconsistent and inefficient. With four bartenders present, I was confounded by their inability to smoothly manage a crowd of roughly forty-five guests. Without dedicated stations, they floated around the circular bar, often stopping just short of my seat to prioritize waitress station orders. This constant rotation made it impossible to establish any rapport or receive attentive service.

Furthermore, the clientele significantly detracted from the atmosphere. The space was dominated by what I can only describe as the typical casino gambler—patrons who seemed to have no interest in the bar itself. If your sole purpose is to play the machines, why not sit directly at one? Their presence felt incongruous. My frustration peaked when an individual sat beside me and lit a cigarette, allowing the smoke to drift directly into my face. While I respect that a public bar is shared space, common courtesy should prevail. If you see your smoke bothering a neighbor, simple consideration—like repositioning an ashtray—isn't too much to ask. The blatant disregard was aggravating.

This entire experience clarified why I value venues like Cin Cin so deeply. Not only do they craft superior cocktails, but they also cultivate an environment dedicated to that experience, free from the intrusion of gambling machines. For the Peppermill to create a genuinely compelling cocktail bar, I would suggest several critical changes: remove the slot machines from the bar area to attract a more appropriate crowd, invest in comprehensive staff training or hire bartenders with proven hospitality skills, and upgrade the liquor selection to include quality, independent spirits. As it stands, the Terrace Lounge feels like an afterthought, not a destination.

input:
Thank you for a lovely morning!  I was in NJ early and decided to stop in for a delicious diner breakfast.  I got a taylor ham, egg, and cheese and a short stack of blueberry pancakes (I simply couldn't decide between sweet or savory, plus leftovers are never a bad thing).  

The egg sandwich was fantastic.  I was nervous when they said they didn't have kaiser rolls so I went with a hamburger roll.  It was an excellent decision.  The roll was excellent - not just an average cheap hamburger roll.  They layered the cheese on the sandwich, which to me is a must for a true egg sandwich.  It was served with home fries, which were sauteed with large slices of peppers and onions.  I'm not the biggest breakfast potatoes fan, but these were great and I appreciated that they didn't clearly just scoop some food from a huge pile of pre-cooked home fries.

The pancakes were great and fluffy.  My one gripe was their use of smuckers pre-packaged syrup.  I realize that if they put syrup in a container, it probably wouldn't be real maple syrup, but I sort of wish I didn't know that they were giving me sub-par syrup.

The server was friendly and very attentive.  The coffee refills were constant, and the coffee was actually good (so many diners fail at coffee).  Bonus points for the server agreeing not to judge my decision to get two breakfasts.

All around, I loved this place and hope to go back soon.  Long live the Jersey diners!
Rewrite this for me:
Thank you for a wonderful morning! I had an early start in New Jersey and chose to swing by for a classic, delicious diner breakfast. Unable to decide between sweet or savory—and knowing leftovers are never a bad thing—I ordered both a Taylor ham, egg, and cheese sandwich and a short stack of blueberry pancakes.

The sandwich was fantastic. Initially, I was hesitant when they said they were out of Kaiser rolls, so I opted for a hamburger bun. This turned out to be an excellent choice; the roll was far above the average, cheap alternative. They layered the cheese perfectly, which I consider essential for a proper egg sandwich. It came with home fries sautéed with large slices of peppers and onions. I’m not usually a big fan of breakfast potatoes, but these were excellent, and I appreciated that they weren’t just scooped from a massive bin of pre-cooked potatoes.

The pancakes were wonderfully fluffy. My only minor complaint was the Smuckers pre-packaged syrup. While I understand that syrup served from a container likely isn’t real maple, part of me wishes I didn’t have the confirmation that it was sub-par.

The server was friendly and very attentive, with constant coffee refills of actually good coffee—a rarity in many diners. Bonus points to her for kindly agreeing not to judge my decision to order two full breakfasts.

All around, I loved this place and hope to return soon. Long live the Jersey diner!

input:
The new Han Dynasty took over the spot where the old Mid-Atlantic restaurant (with the unchanging menu) was. I like the Han Dynasty here a lot more than the one in Olde City even if I give both 4*. Maybe I'm biased, because I love the service here. They've always been very nice, and came over to check in with me and just make some small conversation when they heard I had a peanut allergy (even though they had no peanuts in any of the dishes I ordered; I think it was Han's sister?). I've been to this Han Dynasty more times in a month than the number of times I've been to the other.

Note though, that the different branches have different specialties. I heard the dan dan mian in Olde City is the best, but the one in UC isn't so good (I wouldn't know since it has peanuts). Overall, I think it;s okay food wise, still not spicy enough as with the other branch. But I like the layout and atmosphere a lot more.

Next, if you go during lunch, you can ask for lunch portions, that are smaller than the dinner portions, and half the menu price! So it's a great lunch place too, alone, or in a group of 2 or 3.
Rewrite this for me:
The new Han Dynasty replaced the former Mid-Atlantic restaurant, which was known for its static menu. I strongly prefer this location to the Olde City branch, even though I’d rate both four stars. My bias may stem from the exceptional service here. The staff has always been exceptionally kind, and upon hearing about my peanut allergy, they made a point to check in and engage in friendly conversation—even though my chosen dishes contained no peanuts (I believe it was Han’s sister who stopped by). I’ve visited this location more times in a single month than I’ve ever visited the other.

It’s worth noting that each branch has its own specialties. I’ve heard the dan dan mian at Olde City is superior, while the University City version isn’t as good (I can’t personally verify, as it contains peanuts). Overall, I find the food here okay, though like the other location, it could be spicier. However, I much prefer the layout and atmosphere.

Finally, if you visit during lunch, you can request smaller lunch portions at half the menu price. This makes it an excellent spot for lunch, whether you’re dining alone or with a small group.

input:
We went to Carisma Restaurante again tonight. It has become our "go to" spot. The food is excellent and the service was great. The owner Jose is very friendly and tries to visit every table to make sure everyone is satisfied.  Tonight we had 2 Paellas, salmon and a filet mignon. Everything was made to order, cooked to perfection and came out hot.  

The family also opened a cafe in front of the restaurant. Jose gave us a tour and introduced us to his daughter that runs the cafe. The baked goods and coffees at the cafe are just as good as the meals at Carisma. Good, fresh food prepared and served by nice people. Try Carisma, it's so much more than just the normal tacos and burritos. You wont be disappointed!
Rewrite this for me:
Carisma Restaurante was our destination once more this evening, solidifying its status as our favorite local spot. The food is consistently excellent and the service remains superb. The owner, Jose, is wonderfully friendly, making a point to visit each table to ensure complete satisfaction. Our meal tonight included two paellas, salmon, and a filet mignon. Each dish was made to order, cooked perfectly, and arrived piping hot.

The family has also opened a cafe at the front. Jose gave us a tour and introduced us to his daughter, who manages it. Its baked goods and coffee match the quality of Carisma’s meals. This is simply good, fresh food prepared and served by genuinely nice people. I highly recommend Carisma; it offers so much more than standard tacos and burritos. You will not be disappointed.

input: This is a small hole in the wall in the African section of Woodland Avenue.  Though it might not look like much, there is some good food coming out of its kitchen representing Senegal and West Africa.  I enjoyed the national dish of Senegal - Thiboudienne - although note that here they do a version without the usual tomato sauce.  I also took home a Jollof Rice which is often called the mother dish of Jambalaya.  There are a few hightop tables inside for dining or you can order the food to-go.  Either way, service is friendly.
Rewrite this for me:
Tucked along Woodland Avenue’s African stretch is this modest, hole-in-the-wall spot. Don’t let the simple exterior fool you—the kitchen delivers excellent Senegalese and West African fare. I tried Senegal’s national dish, Thiboudienne, prepared here in a unique, tomato-less version. I also took home a flavorful Jollof Rice, considered a precursor to Jambalaya. A few high-top tables are available for dining in, or you can opt for takeout. Whichever you choose, expect genuinely friendly service.

input: Had a falafel wrap here a few years ago. Not bad, so tried it again today. No flavor, except extreme saltiness! The falafels & pita = no flavor. Rewrite this for me: I tried a falafel wrap here years ago. It was decent, so I gave it another chance today. The result was a total letdown. The only fresh elements were the diced cucumber and tomato, sadly buried under that sorry excuse for a sauce.

input:

Our party of six chose this restaurant for a change of pace, and we were very pleased with the choice. My wife and I split the special, which provided a generous and excellent sampling of the menu.
