input: Husband and I made a mistake and came here on a Lenten Friday. The wait was forever. But since we were already there, might as well suck it up and see what's it all about. We ordered the blackened alligator and oysters for appetizers, the alligator came out within 15 minutes, and it was alright. A bit too greasy. Then another 15 minutes later, our raw oysters came out, I wanted mine char grilled but the waitress didn't mention they don't have char grilled oysters and still took my order, so I thought I was waiting for mine to be cooked the entire time. When she brought out the two half-dozen raw oyster trays, that's when she told me they only have raw oysters there. SMH. I have sensitive stomach so I only had 3 then gave the rest to my husband. Regardless, the oysters were really fresh. We waited for at least another 20 minutes later for our entrees to come out. At this point, I was really hungry and had hoped we were at home eating ramen noodles instead. My husband had the roast beef po-boy, and I had the tuna and shrimp kabob. My husband told me his roast beef was really salty and while ironically, my kabob was very bland. The kabob came with exactly 3 pieces of cubed tuna, 2 medium size shrimp with plenty of bell peppers and onions in between, and baby shrimp creole with rice. For the ok price, I shouldn't complain too much about this place. Didn't try their seafood boil, but it looked like that would have been a better choice.
Rewrite this for me:
My husband and I made the error of visiting on a Friday during Lent. The wait was interminable. However, having already committed, we decided to endure it and see what the restaurant offered.

We started with blackened alligator and oysters. The alligator arrived in about fifteen minutes; it was acceptable, though somewhat overly greasy. Another fifteen minutes later, our raw oysters were delivered. I had actually wanted mine char-grilled, but the waitress had taken the order without mentioning they weren’t available, so I spent the entire wait expecting a cooked dish. She only informed me they served only raw oysters when presenting the two half-dozen trays. I have a sensitive stomach, so I ate just three and gave the remainder to my husband. That said, the oysters were undeniably fresh.

We then waited at least another twenty minutes for our entrees. By then, I was ravenous and wistfully imagining a simple bowl of ramen at home. My husband ordered the roast beef po-boy, which he found excessively salty. Ironically, my tuna and shrimp kabob was quite bland. It contained exactly three cubes of tuna, two medium shrimp, and an abundance of bell peppers and onions, served with a side of baby shrimp creole and rice.

Given the reasonable prices, I shouldn’t complain too much. We didn’t sample the seafood boil, but based on appearances, that might have been the wiser choice.

input:
im going to have to give this place one star for its horrible customer service:

i called in to ask about the 50% off for tulane students they were advertising, the woman assured me if i came with an id it would be half off and made an appointment for me, only once i got there did they tell me it's only on certain days, "it says it right on the sign," i was perturbed by the inconvenience and said so you're not going to honor it even though you just made an appointment with me and told me it would be 50% off, they said no flat out at first even though the error was blatantly on their side, after my nagging, she eventually called john jay himself and he told the woman that he would not honor what i was told even though i had been inconvenienced by someone in HIS staff because it might cause a 'domino effect,' i said how will there be a domino effect unless you continue to give people incorrect information, there will be no other 'dominoes' as long as you remember what day it is from now on... they began to treat me somewhat patronizingly as i explained that usually businesses make concessions when they are the one at fault, that the customer is supposed to always be right, yadda yadda yadda, i left pretty upset and with ~45 minutes of my life having been wasted - empty handed but for a lame excuse from someone who owns at least 3 businesses over 10 dollars...

i have not received a haircut from them so if you're one of those people who ONLY cares about the product and you think you'll get a good cut go right on ahead, but if you're like me (principled) and you don't like handing profits to people who care nothing about their customers this is a good place to skip next time you need a cut
Rewrite this for me:
My experience with this establishment warrants a one-star review due to profoundly poor customer service.

I initially called to inquire about the advertised 50% discount for Tulane students. The woman who answered assured me the discount would apply if I presented my student ID and proceeded to schedule an appointment for me. However, upon my arrival, I was informed the promotion was only valid on specific days, with the employee dismissively noting, "It says it right on the sign." I was understandably upset by this inconvenience and pointed out that they had just confirmed the discount while making my appointment. Their initial response was a flat refusal, despite the error originating entirely from their staff.

After I persisted, the employee contacted the owner, John Jay. He instructed her that he would not honor the promise made to me, citing concern over a potential "domino effect." I countered that such an effect could only occur if they continued to provide incorrect information; correcting their process would prevent any further "dominoes" from falling. Throughout this discussion, their tone became increasingly patronizing. I explained that businesses typically make concessions when they are at fault and that customer satisfaction should be a priority, but my reasoning was met with indifference.

I left feeling deeply frustrated, having wasted roughly 45 minutes and receiving nothing but a feeble excuse from an owner of multiple businesses—all over a matter of $10.

I did not actually receive a haircut here. Therefore, if you are someone who values only the end product and believes you might get a good cut, you could proceed. But if you, like me, operate on principle and prefer not to patronize businesses that demonstrate such disregard for their customers, this is a place you would be wise to avoid for your next haircut.

input: Awesome food, great place to split a bunch of delicious spicy, ultra flavorful dishes with a large group. It's the Chinese restaurant a lot of people know about for good reason - I haven't had a single bad dish here, and it's always a crowd-pleaser.
Rewrite this for me: Perfect for sharing, this popular Chinese restaurant is a crowd-pleaser. Every spicy and flavorful dish I’ve tried has been excellent, making it an ideal spot for a large group to enjoy a memorable meal together.

input:
My friend and I visited Tampa for a concert, and about ten minutes away from the Atlanta airport he realized that he had purchased tickets for the wrong day. We had already made hotel reservations and bought the concert tickets, so he just had to pay same-day price for airfare: all in all about $800 more. "It was totally worth it," he later told me, "Because I got to have the best sandwich of my entire life."

All because we randomly picked the Bricks of Ybor from Yelp. I can't vouch for the peanut butter or meatless menu, but the meat sandwiches that we bought were absolutely phenomenal. I had the pulled pork, which was flavored with ponzu and served on Hawaiian sweet bread. It was one of the best meals I've had in a long time. We spent a few hours hanging out and drinking, during which time Brian, the owner, came out and talked to us, comped us a drink, let us try new appetizers he was developing (all for free) and generally made us feel really welcome. 

I kept my eyes open to the kind of crowd that came in and out of the restaurant. It seemed to draw everything from hipsters to geriatrics and strait-laced families with young kids. I think it speaks to both the diversity of the menu and the pleasant environment. We went back for drinks before and after the concert. It got very crowded but we still received excellent food, drinks and service. I give this restaurant my strongest recommendation, and it's the first place I'm going when I next visit Tampa.
Rewrite this for me:
A trip to Tampa for a concert took an expensive turn when my friend realized, just minutes from the Atlanta airport, that he’d bought our tickets for the wrong day. With hotels and event tickets already secured, he had to swallow the cost of same-day airfare—an extra $800. Yet, he later insisted, “It was totally worth it, because I got to have the best sandwich of my entire life.”

That sandwich came from a random Yelp selection: Bricks of Ybor. While I can’t speak to their peanut butter or meatless options, the meat sandwiches we ordered were phenomenal. I chose the pulled pork, flavored with ponzu and served on Hawaiian sweet bread—one of the best meals I’ve had in years. We lingered for hours, and the owner, Brian, came out to chat, comped us a drink, and offered samples of new appetizers he was developing, all free. His warmth made us feel genuinely welcome.

Observing the crowd, I noticed the place drew everyone from hipsters and seniors to families with young children—a testament to both the diverse menu and the inviting atmosphere. We returned for drinks before and after the concert. Even when packed, the food, service, and quality remained excellent. I give Bricks of Ybor my highest recommendation; it will be my first stop when I’m next in Tampa.

input: So worth the wait! The crepes are amazing! I also loved the grits, which is rare. Tried my hubby's pancakes....awesome!
Rewrite this for me: So worth the wait! The crepes were amazing, and I even loved the grits—rare for me. My husband's pancakes were awesome, too.

input: My sister-in-law and I visited this restaurant on 8/28/15 mid afternoon.  We were seated after requested 3 times that the hostess speak a little louder because we couldn't even hear her with the background music.  We were seated in a booth with a never ending Larry King vitamin commercial on the TV - really?  Our waitress introduced herself and a new trainee and then we never saw her again.  Two other wait staff seemed to be sharing our table, but no idea who was responsible for our table.  We got our drinks and ordered, but food took forever considering there was not more than 15-20 filled tables in the entire restaurant.  Burgers were not bad - I ordered the blue cheese burger and it would have been better with less blue cheese, way too much!  Fries and onion sticks were very good.  But no one came to see if we were satisfied, needing anything, etc and took two requests and waiting to get a carry out box.  There was a family seated across the aisle from us when we arrived and we assumed they had finished their meal and were "hanging out".  Only after we received our food did we understand they had already ordered and still did not have their food!  I doubt I will return to this restaurant in the future.
Rewrite this for me:
My sister-in-law and I dined at this restaurant on the afternoon of August 28, 2015. Our experience began poorly when we had to ask the hostess three times to speak louder over the intrusive background music just to be seated. We were placed in a booth where a television endlessly played a Larry King vitamin commercial—an odd and unwelcome distraction.

Our assigned waitress introduced herself and a trainee, then vanished. Two other servers intermittently attended our table, creating confusion over who was actually responsible for our service. We received our drinks and placed our order, but the food took a remarkably long time to arrive, despite the restaurant being only partially occupied with perhaps 15 to 20 tables filled.

The food was mixed. My blue cheese burger was decent but overwhelmed by an excessive amount of cheese. The fries and onion sticks, however, were quite good. Throughout the meal, service was absent; no one checked on our satisfaction or needs. We had to ask twice and wait extensively for a simple takeaway box.

A telling moment occurred with a family seated nearby. We initially thought they were lingering after a meal, but only after we got our food did we realize they had ordered before us and were still waiting. Given the consistently poor service and mismanagement, it is unlikely I will return.

input:
In short, the food was decently good, but completely overpriced.  The guacamole and my Mojito were probably the highlight of the meal. I had the peach pork medallions, which were nicely cooked, but lacked flavor. I tried the corn cakes with Barbacoa and that was pretty good.  

The atmosphere was inviting with a hip feel if that's what you're looking for.  What was really annoying was the parking situation. For a place with price points such as these and limited parking spaces, a valet service should be provided either at a cost or complimentary.  Don't even try and park in the back of the building, it's tight and dangerous even getting there and back.  I ended up parking three blocks away and broke a sweat walking in the dead of summer to the front entrance.
Rewrite this for me:
The meal was reasonably good, yet decidedly overpriced. Highlights included the fresh guacamole and a well-made Mojito. My peach pork medallions were cooked properly but underwhelming in flavor, while the corn cakes with Barbacoa were a better choice.

The ambiance was inviting and stylish. However, the parking situation was a significant frustration. For a restaurant at this price level with very limited spaces, a valet service—whether complimentary or paid—is a reasonable expectation. The rear lot is dangerously tight and difficult to navigate. I ultimately parked three blocks away and endured a sweltering summer walk to the entrance, which considerably dampened the experience.

Despite a prior reservation specifically requesting a window seat overlooking the water, the hostess initially tried to seat us elsewhere. input:
This was a tough one!   On the merits of the wine, fairly average... I understand that the winery has more than one lable and other label is their premium wines.  I look forward to when that is available (I went two weeks ago so maybe it already is)     Location..   what's not to like?  On the pier!  A wonderful outdoor patio,  couldn't have a nicer setting to enjoy your tasting....   The staff were super, super nice,  I would give them an A+!  

So why only three stars?  It is because of the wine club!  Very expensive for the quality of the wines and stingy as HELL with the benefits to the members..   Most wine clubs will give you a free tasting every time you come in (after all, we are your best customers... we are the ones who buy your wine time and time again).  Some wineries will give their members a complimentary glass in leau of a tasting (Carr).   Most wineries allow you to bring guests which is how you get new wine club members.   This system works folks!  The way this wine club works is that you are given a very limited number of passes per quarter, five as I recall.   If I come with my wife once a month we wouldn't even be covered... let alone if we bring a guest!   

So go to this winery if you want to enjoy a tasting in one of the most beautiful settings on earth.   But avoid the wine club!  For that you can pretty much go to any of the other wine tasting rooms on the Urban wine trail.
Rewrite this for me:
This was a challenging review to write. Based purely on the wine quality, my experience was fairly average. I understand the winery produces another label for its premium offerings, and I look forward to trying those when available (I visited two weeks ago, so perhaps they are now).

The location, however, is exceptional—right on the pier! The wonderful outdoor patio provides a stunning setting for a tasting, which couldn’t be nicer. Additionally, the staff were superb and incredibly friendly; they truly deserve an A+.

So, why only three stars? The reason is the wine club. It is very expensive relative to the quality of the wines and surprisingly stingy with member benefits. Most clubs offer a complimentary tasting with each visit, recognizing that members are their best, repeat customers. Some wineries even provide a complimentary glass in lieu of a tasting. Crucially, most encourage members to bring guests, as that is a primary way to attract new members—a system that works well elsewhere.

This club’s structure is far more restrictive. Members receive a very limited number of passes per quarter—five, as I recall. That wouldn’t even cover monthly visits with my spouse, let alone allow us to bring a guest.

Therefore, I recommend visiting this winery to enjoy a tasting in one of the most beautiful settings imaginable. But I would advise avoiding the wine club. For a club membership, you can find better value and hospitality at almost any other tasting room on the Urban Wine Trail.

DROOL.

Love this place!!!

An absolute favorite!

input:
--------DINNER REVIEW----------

I rarely write reviews, but this honestly was one of the worst group dining experiences I've ever had. It was objectively a horrible experience, even without comparing it to the hype it receives, and ruined what was supposed to be a nice birthday dinner celebration. 

We had a group of 8 that had a reservation made well in advance. Short wait, but not too bad. Keep in mind, it seemed like a normal Friday night, but weren't super busy or at-capacity.

It was a birthday dinner, so I told the hostesses that it was her birthday, and asked if they could bring out something for her at the end of the meal, which was acknowledged. Pretty standard stuff, whether at a Applebee's or the French Laundry. We were sat at a booth right next to the Maitre D' stand, and next to all the wait staff's home base, so pretty much no excuse for not getting any attention. 

After getting us waters, it took them a LONG time to even come by and acknowledge us. After ordering wine, it took them another good 15-20 minutes to even bring us our wine, and no one even checked in on us! (hint: if you're running a restaurant, wine is your profit center and doesn't take any work other than taking a bottle off a shelf and opening it. bring it out ASAP...). 

After ordering food, it was more of the same...a long wait for food to start coming out and no one checking in on us AT ALL. We drank the bottles we ordered and had to get up and flag someone down to get another wine order. A couple of us even got up during the meal to remind them to bring out something for birthday girl at the end of the meal. 

Once our meal was done and taken away, we were given dessert menus and the server disappeared for 10-15 minutes... AGAIN. After coming back, he asked what dessert we wanted, so we ordered some coffees... and waited... and waited. Eventually we got up and asked him what was going on and if they were going to bring anything out like we asked multiple times. 

They finally brought out a couple of cookies with a candle...

In summary, the food was pretty hit or miss, pretty mediocre for this price point. Whipped feta, like other reviews have said, was amazing, and the Braised Lamb was really good. But the Sirloin was chewy and bland and the Grilled Caesar tasted like a soggy, luke-warm, wilted mess (two orders were left untouched by a group of 8). Atmosphere was nice and trendy. But the service, which is a huge reason to spend your hard-earned $ at a restaurant, was absolutely horrendous. 

I really love going to cool, popular restaurants and having a great time, and I hate writing such a negative review, but I had to share my experience, especially for a restaurant that is getting an awful lot of (undeserved) hype.
Rewrite this for me:
--------DINNER REVIEW----------

I seldom write reviews, but this was genuinely one of the most disappointing group dining experiences I can recall. Objectively, it was a horrible evening that ruined a planned birthday celebration, independent of the considerable hype surrounding this restaurant.

Our party of eight had a reservation made well in advance. We experienced a short wait upon arrival, which was acceptable. The restaurant appeared to be having a typical Friday night—busy, but not at capacity.

Having booked a birthday dinner, I informed the hostesses of the occasion and requested a small gesture for the guest of honor at the meal’s conclusion—a standard practice acknowledged by the staff. We were seated at a booth immediately adjacent to the Maître D' stand and the primary service station, placing us at the very heart of the floor. This location made the subsequent neglect inexcusable.

After initial waters were provided, there was a prolonged delay before we were even acknowledged. We ordered wine, and then waited another 15-20 minutes for the bottles to arrive, with no check-in in the interim. A basic tenet of restaurant service is to prioritize wine, a key profit driver requiring minimal preparation.

The pattern continued after ordering food. Courses arrived after lengthy intervals, again with zero proactive check-ins from any server. We finished our wine and had to physically flag down a staff member to order more. During the meal, several of us even had to get up to remind them about the birthday acknowledgment.

Once our plates were cleared and dessert menus provided, our server vanished for another 10-15 minutes. Upon his return, we ordered coffee and dessert, only to be met with another extended wait. We finally rose to inquire about the delay and, again, about the forgotten birthday gesture.

The acknowledgment, when it finally came, was a couple of cookies with a candle.

In summary, the food was inconsistent and mediocre for the price point. As other reviews note, the whipped feta was excellent, and the braised lamb was very good. However, the sirloin was chewy and bland, and the grilled Caesar salad arrived as a soggy, lukewarm, wilted mess—two full orders remained untouched by our group of eight. Yet service is a fundamental reason for spending hard-earned money at a restaurant, and here it was utterly horrendous. I take no pleasure in writing such a negative assessment, but I feel compelled to share this experience, particularly for an establishment receiving so much—and in my view, undeserved—acclaim.

input:
Second stop for Center City Restaurant Week:  R2L, dinner for $35 each. 

On the 37th floor of Two Liberty Place is a very fancy-cool restaurant/lounge where you can get a bird's eye view of the city! Group of us went to dinner here together after a day of meetings. Didn't get one of the tables facing the windows, but still had great views of the sunset and city by night. Again, multiple choices for the three courses, but I chose to start with the crisp peas/ham/garlic risotto [balls]. Main course was the Butcher's Filet (braised short rib + Steuben bean chili, potato/farm veg slaw and basil), which was quite heavy since there was also meat in the chili as well. The dazzling dessert to finish it off was the milk chocolate + hazelnut pudding served with salted caramel and coffee to melt the chocolate, and candied almonds on the side. A bottle of wine for the table as well. Food was great, waiter was awesome (making sure to warn me that the risotto came in ball form rather than a bowl, for instance), very classy experience.
Rewrite this for me:
Our second stop for Center City Restaurant Week was R2L, where the fixed-price dinner offered a three-course meal for $35 per person.

Located on the 37th floor of Two Liberty Place, the restaurant is a sophisticated lounge with breathtaking, bird’s-eye views of Philadelphia. Our group dined there after a day of meetings. Although we weren’t seated directly at the window, we still enjoyed a spectacular sunset that faded into a glittering city nightscape.

From the multiple options for each course, I began with the crisp peas, ham, and garlic risotto balls. For the main, I chose the Butcher’s Filet—a braised short rib served with Steuben bean chili (which contained additional meat), a potato and farm vegetable slaw, and basil. It was a decidedly hearty dish. The meal concluded with a dazzling dessert: milk chocolate and hazelnut pudding accompanied by salted caramel, a side of coffee to melt the chocolate, and candied almonds.

We also shared a bottle of wine. The food was excellent, and our waiter was attentive—even thoughtfully clarifying that the risotto came as balls, not in a bowl. Overall, it was a truly classy experience.

input:
I moved from Chicago to Philadelphia over a year ago.  Everybody here raves about the restaurants, but I have yet to find many that deserve five stars, or even four.  This is the best restaurant I have eaten in in Philadelphia.  

Tahini and bread  arrived at the table, and I thought, hum, plain but I'm hungry.  They must put crack in that Tahini.  I wanted to lap it out of the bowl like an uncouth dog.  The bread is excellent too.

I love a menu with many organic meat choices.  How often can you order an organic beef shishkabob?  It was superb.  The meat done perfectly, the onions nearly caramelized but not quite so they still had some substantive crunch.  The purslane salad tasted like I was eating a plant in the middle of a garden.  It is not often that I dream about a salad but I do dream about this one

My husband had a chicken dish with black eyed peas and green peas and fantastic rice.  I won't begin to describe the flavoring; it is beyond my culinary vocabulary.  We asked what spices they use, and in addition to traditional zatar, they use their own blend of spices.  I don't even need to know what is in it just so long as we can keep coming back and ordering it again and again.

I was so full but ate dessert none the less, which I usually don't do.  But when a diner is this good, I had a feeling the desserts would be too and I just needed to find out.  Pistachio creme brulee.  It could have come out over the top, but no indeed.  It was pure pistachio heaven in s super light yet rich custard.  Heaven. Heaven.

Our service was superb.  The squeezed us into a last minute Friday night reservation with the caveat that we would need to get through our dinner in an hour and 15 minutes in order to accommodate a reservation made prior to us.  Given the time constraints they never made us feel rushed and timed the meal perfectly.  Then my husband left to go to the restroom, the waiter picked up his napkin and refolded it nicely on the table.  Do I care about the napkin placement in the middle of a meal?  Not really, but it is a sign that the waitstaff is incredibly attentive and extremely well trained.  

My eating out plan for Philly might just be to skip eating most everywhere most of the time so I can frequent this expensive, though appropriately priced restaurant.  Kudos to the chef.
Rewrite this for me:
Having lived in Philadelphia for just over a year, I’ve heard constant praise for the city’s dining scene. Yet, in my experience, few establishments have truly earned a four- or five-star rating. This restaurant is the exception—it is, without question, the best meal I have had since moving here.

Our meal began simply with tahini and bread. My initial thought was that it seemed plain, but hunger prevailed. That first taste changed everything. The tahini was so inexplicably delicious I nearly considered lapping it from the bowl. The accompanying bread was equally excellent.

I was immediately drawn to a menu featuring numerous organic meat options—a rarity. I chose the organic beef shishkabob, and it was superb. The meat was cooked perfectly, and the onions were nearly caramelized while retaining a satisfying, substantive crunch. The purslane salad tasted astonishingly fresh, as if plucked straight from a garden. It is not often I dream about a salad, but I find myself dreaming of this one.

My husband ordered a chicken dish served with black-eyed peas, green peas, and fantastic rice. The flavor profile was so complex it defies my culinary vocabulary. When we inquired about the spices, we learned they use a proprietary blend in addition to traditional za’atar. Frankly, I don’t need to know what’s in it—I only need to know we can return to order it again and again.

Despite being full, I felt compelled to try dessert—a departure from my usual habit. When a meal is this exceptional, you suspect the desserts will follow suit. The pistachio crème brûlée confirmed it. It could have been overly rich, but instead it was a perfect balance: pure pistachio essence in a superbly light yet rich custard. It was, simply, heaven.

The service matched the quality of the food. They accommodated a last-minute Friday night reservation with the caveat that we would need to conclude within an hour and fifteen minutes. Despite this constraint, we never felt rushed; each course was timed perfectly. At one point, my husband stepped away, and our waiter discreetly picked up his napkin, refolding it neatly on the table. While napkin placement mid-meal isn’t something I typically notice, it signaled an incredibly attentive and well-trained staff.

My strategy for dining out in Philadelphia may now be to forgo meals elsewhere, saving both appetite and budget for this restaurant. It is certainly expensive, but every bite justifies the price. My highest compliments to the chef.

input:
Uhhhhh.... Not sure how to quantify or qualify my experience here. Let's start with back story: 

My sister was visiting for the weekend, so I wanted to show her a solid night on the town that lasted till the wee hours of the morning. We started on Frenchmen, but for whatever reason it was dead. 
Deciding to adventure Uptown we proceeded on a respectable bar crawl, including Delachaise, Columns, and St. Joes, however, at 3 AM the usual Uptown culprits start to raise their heads. A summary of the following dialogue:

Friends "Let's go to FMs" 
Me: "No, too much broken glass"
Friends: "Let's go to Snake and Jake's"
Me: "Eh...."
Friends: "Brothers 3?"
Me: "I'm afraid I'll hit my head on the ceiling"
Friends: "The Saint!!"
Me: "I suppose I haven't been there before, I'm curious."

After entering the Saint the look on my sisters face was priceless, akin to a deer in headlights look. I kept my countenance, and we ordered a round. Things proceeded as expected ... unwanted dance grinding advances, check! uber drunk guy talking your ear off, check! Big Buck Hunter, CHECK!!! Overall I'm glad I moderately traumatized my sister and sated my curiosity in the same night. 

Helpful hint: They have outdoor seating, surprisingly, which is very good to escape the smoke
Rewrite this for me:
I’m not entirely sure how to quantify or qualify my experience here, so I’ll begin with some context.

My sister was visiting for the weekend, and I wanted to give her a proper night out that stretched into the early morning. We started on Frenchmen Street, but it was unexpectedly quiet. We decided to head Uptown and embarked on a respectable bar crawl, hitting spots like Delachaise, the Columns, and St. Joe’s. By 3 a.m., however, the usual late-night Uptown options began to surface. The ensuing conversation went something like this:

Friends: “Let’s go to F&M’s.”  
Me: “No, too much broken glass.”  
Friends: “How about Snake and Jake’s?”  
Me: “Eh…”  
Friends: “Brothers Three?”  
Me: “I’m afraid I’ll hit my head on the ceiling.”  
Friends: “The Saint!”  
Me: “I haven’t been there before—I’m curious.”

Once inside The Saint, my sister’s expression was priceless—a true deer-in-headlights look. I kept my composure, and we ordered a round. The rest unfolded predictably: unwanted dance-floor advances, check; an overly drunk guy talking your ear off, check; Big Buck Hunter, check. All in all, I’m glad I managed to moderately traumatize my sister while satisfying my curiosity in one night.

A helpful tip: they have outdoor seating, which is a surprisingly good escape from the indoor smoke.

input:
I stopped by Bell Meade during a recent visit to Nashville. The best way for me to describe my experience is to say that the next time I go to Nashville I will go out of my way to make sure I return to Bell Meade.

On my travels, I tend to stop from time to time to see if I can find specific bourbons that may be out locally. At this time of year, I did not expect any great finds because many of the items for which I look have their annual release later in the year so it's a surprise to find any of them on the shelf. For example, Elmer T Lee is a favorite of mine so it was one that I asked about.

Despite the fact that I walked away without Elmer T, I still had a great time. I enjoyed a few tastes at the tasting bar and even better I had a great conversation with Max. He is one of the reasons I will return.

Given the time of year, my expectations were low; many of the annual releases I seek arrive later in the fall, so discovering any on the shelf is a genuine surprise. While I left without that particular bottle, the experience was thoroughly enjoyable. I sampled a few offerings at the tasting bar and, even better, had a fantastic conversation with Max. His knowledge and hospitality are a primary reason I plan to go back.

My visit was still fruitful. I purchased a bottle of Tennessee whiskey cream unavailable in my area, and I spotted another shelf item I haven’t seen locally and need to research further. That I intend to return says it all, and my five-star rating stands as a full endorsement.

input:
I love trying fresh seafood on piers, wharfs and seaside markets. Most of the time, it is a disappointing experience but this place is not. The food is legitimately fresh and prepared well. The gorgeous view is just a cherry on top of nature's beautiful sundae. I have been here before but ordered the "wrong" thing (cioppino). That wasn't very good when I had it a couple of years ago here. 

We came for a late lunch/early dinner on a Monday. Even at 4pm,  there was a wait! We waited about 25 minutes and got a table outdoor. While it wasn't ideal that we sat right in the sun with no shelter other than our sunscreen and sunglasses, the view was worth it. 

We got the local crab special which was a steamed 3-lb. crab served with a salad and soup for $26. I thought this was quite the steal because the crab was huge, delicious and meaty. The garden salad was fresh as simple as it was. The lobster bisque we got was pretty good. (The other options were Caesar salad and clam chowder). They topped off the crab with a couple of onion rings and cups of cocktail sauce and drawn butter. Yum!

We also got the fried platter of shrimp, oysters, calamari and scallops for $12.95. It came with cole slaw, onion rings, tartar sauce and cocktail sauce. As greasy of a meal as this made, it was one of the better fried platters I've had anywhere. The seafood was just really fresh including the sometimes-feared fried oyster. :)

The ice in our iced teas melted away in the sun. Our waitress was so cool and brought us lots of extra ice and an extra iced tea in case we needed it (we did because it was hot out!). She was just friendly and good at her job - five stars for her!

By the time we left at about 6, there were so many people waiting. Make sure you sign up for a seat on the clipboard right when you get there. The restaurant is the last one at the very end of the pier. Parking on the pier is free for 90 minutes but it looks like a drive that will upset tires. I parked in the large lot south of the pier and walked 15 minutes up and onto the pier. It was free on a Monday late afternoon.
Rewrite this for me:
I am a devoted enthusiast of piers, wharfs, and seaside markets, always in pursuit of fresh seafood. More often than not, the experience falls short of expectation, but this establishment is a glorious exception. Here, the food is authentically fresh and skillfully prepared. The stunning panoramic view is merely the perfect cherry on top of nature’s beautiful sundae. I had visited once before but made a poor choice by ordering the cioppino, which was underwhelming several years ago.

We arrived for a late lunch verging on early dinner on a Monday. Even at 4 p.m., there was a waitlist—a testament to its popularity. After about twenty-five minutes, we secured an outdoor table. Although our seating placed us directly in the sun with only sunscreen and sunglasses for protection, the breathtaking vista made the minor discomfort entirely worthwhile.

Our first selection was the local crab special: a steamed three-pound crab served with a salad and soup for twenty-six dollars. This proved to be an exceptional value. The crab was enormous, flavorful, and packed with meat. The accompanying garden salad was crisp and refreshing in its simplicity, and the lobster bisque we chose was quite satisfying. (Alternatives included a Caesar salad or clam chowder.) The plate was finished with a few onion rings and cups of cocktail sauce and drawn butter. Absolutely delicious.

We also ordered the fried seafood platter, priced at twelve ninety-five, which included shrimp, oysters, calamari, and scallops. It came with coleslaw, onion rings, tartar sauce, and cocktail sauce. While this made for an admittedly indulgent meal, it ranked among the best fried platters I have encountered anywhere. Each component was notably fresh—even the sometimes-intimidating fried oyster was excellent.

The sun rapidly melted the ice in our iced teas. Our waitress, however, was wonderfully attentive, promptly bringing us ample extra ice and even a supplemental iced tea, which we gratefully accepted given the heat. Her combination of friendliness and efficiency deserves a full five-star rating.

By our departure around 6 p.m., the crowd had grown substantially. I strongly recommend signing the waitlist clipboard immediately upon arrival. The restaurant is situated at the very end of the pier. While pier parking is free for ninety minutes, the road surface appears rather rough. I opted for the large lot south of the pier and enjoyed a fifteen-minute stroll onto the pier itself—parking there was free on a Monday late afternoon.

input:
What a disappointment. This place was not good I would suggest you think twice before selecting this option. The manager and wait staff may possibly be the worst I have ever encountered, rude and definitely not focused on customer service.  The manager is a very angry hostile fella I asked if I could get brown rice instead of white and he blasted me...I offered to pay extra and he stormed off? Do not know what the deal was but this is just plain unprofessional and creepy behavior. The waitresses will smack into you while you are eating...man what a mess this place is from top to bottom.
The food just OK at best! I am seriously complimenting them here... you can do better at home than here. Seriously I am not going to go into you have been warned just yuk...OK? these other folks with the positive reviews for this place must burn off their taste buds with adult beverages. (Didn't try the sake it may be the high point of the joint...but why would I want to expose my taste buds to a substandard meal to enjoy some rice wine? I can do this at home.
 Here is something I am not sure of, I have only lived here a few months now, is it customary to charge for each soda every time you get a refill here? I was charged for each I asked why they said "This is how we do it here." So at $2 bucks per 6-8 ounces of beverage you may want to go with water at this place...but smarter yet! Go elsewhere.
I will not be returning to this establishment.

Worst yet.
Rewrite this for me:
I was thoroughly disappointed with my experience and would strongly advise you to consider other options before choosing this restaurant. The service was arguably the worst I have ever encountered, with a manager and waitstaff who were remarkably rude and indifferent to customer satisfaction. The manager, in particular, was hostile and unprofessional. When I simply asked about substituting brown rice for white, he reacted with anger. Even my offer to pay extra prompted him to storm away—a baffling and unsettling response. The waitresses were no better, clumsily bumping into our table while we were eating. The entire operation feels chaotic from top to bottom.

As for the food, it was mediocre at best. I am being generous by calling it "just OK"; you could easily prepare a better meal at home. I find it hard to understand the positive reviews from other diners, unless they have completely numbed their taste buds with alcohol beforehand. I didn’t try the sake, which might be the establishment's only redeeming feature, but why would I endure a subpar meal just for a drink I can have elsewhere?

Additionally, I was surprised to be charged for every single soda refill—a practice they defended by saying, "This is how we do it here." At two dollars for each small 6-8 ounce pour, you’re better off sticking with water. In fact, you’re wisest to dine somewhere else entirely.

I will not be returning to this establishment. Worst of all, the overall experience was not just bad, but genuinely unpleasant.

input:
I stayed at the Orange St location from Friday to Monday.

Arrival: I already read plenty of reviews about no signs marking the location therefore, I looked for Starbucks. I parked in a spot in front of the multi business complex. I went inside to find a guard at a desk that said we have been contracted to hand guests their keys and room number and nothing more. He advised me there was a phone that was on the wall that I could make a call to someone if I needed to. He also stated that the very few parking spots in front were free* only on the weekend.

The Room: This wasn't a room, this was an apartment and I absolutely loved it. It was very spacious and had everything I sought* after for that weekend, such as: fully stocked kitchen, a desk, lots of space, king bed, huge table, nice living room, lots of closets. My only complaint is that I could not open any windows for fresh air...they are nailed/screwed shut. There was also a small welcome bag w cookies and water and papers letting you know where all the food delivery locations and numbers.
There wasn't maid service knocking loudly or trying to barge in early in the morning. This place is more of a long term setting and I'm sure the maids come around during the week Monday-Friday if you desire. I was only here for 3 days and I was fine with that. I went shopping at Shoprite and filled my fridge with water and breakfast to cook.

Overall: This place is awesome, I had a huge living room to entertain my guests when they visited, and a nice desk to study my Anatomy notes. I forgot to mention how quiet** this place is. I loved it. I felt as if no one was there except me. Very quiet* which worked for me on Sunday bc I had lots of studying to do and two TV's to watch The Walking Dead on. Lol!  I would most definitely stay here again. Very spacious and updated. Loved it!
Rewrite this for me:
I stayed at the Orange Street location from Friday through Monday.

**Arrival:** Having read numerous reviews noting the lack of signage, I looked for the adjacent Starbucks. I parked in a spot in front of the multi-business complex and went inside. A guard at the desk informed me that his company was only contracted to distribute keys and room numbers. He pointed out a wall phone to call if I needed assistance and noted that the limited front parking spots were complimentary only on weekends.

**The Room:** This was far more than a room—it was a full apartment, and I absolutely loved it. It was incredibly spacious and had everything I needed: a fully stocked kitchen, a desk, a king bed, a large dining table, a comfortable living room, and ample closet space. My sole complaint was that the windows were sealed shut, preventing fresh air. A small welcome bag contained cookies, water, and information with local food delivery options. I appreciated the absence of early morning maid service disruptions; this is clearly geared toward longer-term stays, with service likely available on weekdays. For my three-day stay, it was perfect. I shopped at Shoprite to stock the fridge with water and breakfast items.

**Overall:** This place is awesome. The enormous living room was ideal for entertaining visiting guests, and the desk provided a great space to study my Anatomy notes. I must also emphasize how remarkably quiet the building is. I often felt I had the entire place to myself. The peace was especially welcome on Sunday, allowing for focused study and the luxury of watching *The Walking Dead* on two televisions. The unit was very spacious, modern, and updated. I would definitely stay here again. Loved it!

input: I had the worst experience of my life and it's not over yet.  I made a mistake in purchasing a vehicle that is out of my budget on a Friday afternoon.  By Sunday after review of my budget I realized I was unable to afford the car.  I called the salesman and tried to explain my situation at 11:30am.  He stated he would speak with his manager and call me back.  At 3:30 after no return call, I called him again, no answer. I left a voicemail and still no call at closing time.  Monday morning I arrived at the dealership as they were opening.  I asked Stephen, the salesman what they determined.  He instructed me to have a seat and he would talk to his management team.  One hour + later, I was called into a cubicle and told my loan had been funded and the title had been changed.  Therefore, I would have to sell the car back to the dealership as a used car.  I would lose a lot of money in doing this.  This morning, Bill head of finance advised that the bank had questions about funding the loan.  I received a call from the bank stating the loan had NOT been funded and they would be unable to okay the loan.  I have left numerous messages with the dealership and have yet to receive a callback.  I contacted an attorney and per his review I again called the dealership and asked for a time to return the vehicle and take back my trade.  Still no response!  These people will lie to your face, avoid this dealership!!
Rewrite this for me:
I am enduring one of the most difficult experiences of my life, and it remains unresolved. It began when I made the error of purchasing a vehicle beyond my budget on a Friday afternoon. After reviewing my finances by Sunday, I realized I could not afford it. I called the salesman at 11:30 a.m. to explain my situation. He said he would consult his manager and call me back. By 3:30 p.m., with no callback, I tried him again. There was no answer, so I left a voicemail. The dealership closed without any contact.

I arrived as they opened on Monday morning and asked the salesman, Stephen, for an update. He told me to have a seat while he spoke with management. Over an hour later, I was called into a cubicle and informed that my loan had been funded and the vehicle’s title had been transferred. Their solution was for me to sell the car back to them as a used vehicle, which would mean a significant financial loss.

I have been a patron of Desi Village in West Philly for years.  After moving the suburbs, we saw the KOP Desi Village and finally tried it.  We were skeptical having also tried Mood Cafe (owned by the W.Philly folks), and it wasn't as good. But the KOP location is actually very comparable to the West Philly location.  

There is no ambiance or atmosphere here.  The strip mall where it's located is pretty depressing.  Desi Village may be the only active store in it.  And its decor is tired and old.  It is a big space and it appears they do a big lunch buffet but I'm curious if it's ever full.  So don't go for the ambiance.

But the food is good.  We ordered some Keema Naan, Samosas, Saag Paneer, and Lamb Biryani.  All of it was really good.  Perfectly seasoned, not too oily, and appropriately spicy.  I have a nut allergy and made them aware of that and they did not screw it up (most Indian restaurants do).  So we'll definitely be back.  It would be great if they moved into nicer digs but the food is what is most important.

We were initially skeptical, having also tried Mood Cafe—another venture from the West Philly owners—which didn’t measure up. However, the KOP Desi Village proved to be genuinely comparable to the original in quality.

Do not come here for ambiance. The restaurant sits in a rather bleak strip mall, possibly the only active business within it. The interior decor feels dated and worn. It’s a large space that seems set up for a busy lunch buffet, though I wonder if it ever fills up. Atmosphere is clearly not the draw.

The food, however, is excellent. We ordered Keema Naan, Samosas, Saag Paneer, and Lamb Biryani. Everything was perfectly seasoned, not overly oily, and had just the right level of spice. As someone with a nut allergy, I especially appreciated their careful attention; they handled it flawlessly, which many Indian restaurants often do not. We will definitely return. While a nicer setting would be welcome, the quality of the meal is what matters most.

After today's lunch, Iris has moved to the top of my New Orleans favorites lists--no small feat in a city where restaurants are numerous and culinary competition is fierce. Iris excels in every area: food, drinks, service, atmosphere, location, music and overall graciousness. I made the reservation for 10-15 people, not knowing exactly how many in my party would show up. Iris pulled out all the stops to make sure everyone had comfortable seating and even prepared an overflow table for us. At no time did we feel jostled or rushed, which is a common fine dining concern. 

The layout of the restaurant allowed diners to move freely to and from the table and to exchange seats as needed. The music selection was fun and unique, ranging from the Magnetic Fields to Johnny Cash. It was also quiet enough to be enjoyed while allowing conversation to flow unimpeded. Our waiter had excellent timing and anticipated our every need. 

Though they don't have a full drink menu for lunch (I hear they have an amazing mixologist for the dinner hour) they do offer a selection of martinis and wines. One of the guests has accounts with several high-end bars in the Quarter, and the drink list passed his muster. Our table settled for Chardonnays, Perseco and chilled shots of Chartreuse, though I hear they have several types of absinthe as well. 

Our group began with slices of warm, heavenly bread that Iris bakes in house. We continued with an assortment of salads--I had the Hollygrove arugula with warm goat cheese, niçoise olives and balsamic vinaigrette. It was fresh perfection. A few of us opted for the mussels, which I heard were delicious. For my main course, I had a wonderful drum with onions prepared in a tangy soy reduction, which was an elegant complement for the fish. I also heard rave reviews about the gnocci and chicken. 

All the entrees were creatively arranged and selected, and at no point did I feel overwhelmed or that any fuss or pretense had gone into the food. I also appreciated that the portions were European-sized (it always makes me laugh when other Americans list too-small portion size as a complaint even when the food is well-prepared!). Iris prepares a lot of their basic ingredients in-house, and I appreciate that the kitchen makes a point of incorporating gulf fish and produce purchased from local, farmer-friendly markets. 

We settled on the prix fixe menu, which was $20 a person for appetizer, main course and the dessert of the day (the best strawberry sorbet I have had yet). With the added drinks and tip it came out to under $35 a person, which is an excellent price for such a delicious white-linen lunch. No matter the size of my group, I will definitely be returning!

input:
Another great annual festival Edmonton has to offer.

The Fringe is over two weekends and the joining week full of performances. There's a variety of venues and plays to watch, street performers and musicians. There's a schedule online to find show times, buy tickets and learn more about the artists. 

Half of 104th closes down to add space for a variety of food vendors and artisan vendors (art, jewelry, clothing, etc.).

Good tip: there's a gourmet mini donut truck off behind the farmers market a bit tucked away. Amazing!

It's nice to take an hour or two before or after a show to walk around and casually stumble on other street performances. Or even go without seeing a play just to snack and shop at the vendors.

The location is absolutely fabulous.

A great spot to take out-of-town guests. I take all my Chicago friends here and they fall in love. The burgers are incredible and the boozy shakes are like no other. The first time I had horchata shake I honestly had dreams about it for like a week. It's also super centrally located, a quick walk from Wash Ave and other downtown attractions. Great vibe, although I always prefer to get a table upstairs than sit at the community tables on the ground floor.

The burger selection is really, really great. You can pretty much get whatever your heart desires. I've had mac n cheese patties on my burger, you can get a bison burger, turkey burger, literally anything. I have tried a ton and have never been let down by the flavor combinations. The waiters are always super honest, in a good way. If you ask them what's better, X or Y, they're not going to jerk you around and say they're equally good. They'll give you their honest opinion. LOVE that. 

Another unique aspect about Bailey's Range is that they have a burger showdown (can't remember their technical term for it) where last week's featured burger goes up against a new burger recipe. It's a cool call-out that you don't see at a lot of other restaurants. 

The only reason I gave it a 4/5 star instead of 5/5 is because I've had a couple of instances (out of MANY visits, so it's really not alarming or anything) where I requested my burger medium or medium-rare and it turned out a little well done. I still ate it, but it wasn't really what I expected.

Its central location is a major plus, just a short walk from Washington Avenue and other downtown attractions. The burger selection is outstanding in its variety. Whether you’re craving a classic beef patty, one topped with mac and cheese, a bison burger, or a turkey burger, you can find pretty much anything your heart desires. I’ve tried numerous combinations and have never been disappointed by the flavors. Another fun feature is their weekly burger showdown (I forget their exact name for it), where the previous week’s featured burger competes against a new recipe. It’s a creative touch you don’t see at many other restaurants.
